**Pollen Street carves out Finastra's Universal Banking business**

*The private equity firm's acquisition of Finastra's core banking platform marks the second major disposal from Finastra this year, continuing the break-up of one of Europe's largest banking software groups.*

Pollen Street Capital has agreed to acquire Finastra's Universal Banking unit, which serves banks with Essence, a cloud-native core banking platform. The deal is the second significant divestiture from Finastra, which has been restructuring under pressure from its private equity owners to reduce debt and sharpen its portfolio.

The unit being sold provides core banking technology to financial institutions seeking to modernise legacy infrastructure. Essence positions itself as an open banking-enabled platform, making it relevant to banks navigating PSD2 compliance and open finance readiness. Pollen Street, which has form in financial technology investments, will take on the business as a standalone operation.

For European banks relying on Finastra's universal banking stack, the ownership change raises practical questions about product roadmap continuity, investment levels and strategic direction. Finastra's ongoing break-up also reshapes the competitive landscape for core banking vendors in Europe, where consolidation among platform providers has accelerated.

*Sources: [Pollen Street acquires Finastra's Universal Banking unit](https://ibsintelligence.com/ibsi-news/pollen-street-acquires-finastras-universal-banking-unit/) — IBS Intelligence | [Finastra Lines Up Second Banking Software Sale With Universal Banking Deal](https://fintechnews.sg/133391/digital-banking-news-singapore/finastra-universal-banking/) — Fintech News Singapore*

**Zodia Custody secures EU payment institution licence in Luxembourg**

*The crypto custodian backed by Standard Chartered and Northern Trust has won a payment institution licence from Luxembourg's CSSF, giving it a regulated gateway to offer payment services across the EU.*

Zodia Custody, the institutional digital asset platform whose shareholders include Standard Chartered, Northern Trust, SBI Holdings, National Australia Bank and Emirates NBD, has been granted a payment institution licence by Luxembourg's financial regulator. The licence allows Zodia to provide regulated payment services within the EU, extending its reach beyond pure custody.

The move reflects a broader pattern of institutional crypto infrastructure firms seeking European payment licences to bridge digital assets and conventional payment rails. For Zodia, the licence complements its existing custody operations and positions it to offer end-to-end services — holding assets and facilitating the fiat settlement that institutions require.

Luxembourg continues to attract digital asset firms seeking EU market access, alongside Ireland and the Netherlands. The CSSF licence gives Zodia passporting rights, which matters as MiCA implementation tightens the requirements for crypto service providers operating across member states.

*Sources: [Zodia Custody secures payment license in Luxembourg](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110189/zodia-custody-secures-payment-license-in-luxembourg) — Finextra*

**Egypt's banks complete migration to ISO 20022 for financial transfers**

*The Central Bank of Egypt has confirmed that all banks operating in the country have adopted ISO 20022, joining a global migration that underpins interoperability with European instant payment and open banking infrastructure.*

Egypt's banking sector has completed its adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging standard for financial transfers, according to the Central Bank of Egypt. The regulator described the migration as foundational for next-generation services such as open banking and advanced data analytics, and as essential for alignment with international payment systems.

The move brings Egypt into line with the standard that SWIFT, the Eurosystem and the UK's Pay.UK have adopted or are migrating towards. For European payment processors and correspondent banks with Egyptian counterparts, the switch should improve data quality in cross-border transactions, reducing the friction and manual intervention that older message formats require.

ISO 20022 adoption across emerging markets is relevant to European firms because richer, structured data in payment messages supports sanctions screening, fraud detection and straight-through processing. Each country that completes migration reduces a point of friction in the global payment network.

*Sources: [Banks Operating in Egypt Adopt International ISO 20022 Standard for Financial Transfers](https://www.cbe.org.eg/en/news-publications/news/2026/06/21/08/03/iso-2026) — Central Bank of Egypt | [Egypt upgrades banking system to global ISO 20022 standard](https://english.ahram.org.eg/News/571269.aspx) — Ahram Online*
